ai.description: This slender snake reaches 30 cm. It is pale brown above with a dark vertebral stripe and a black-tipped tail. A distinctive black nuchal collar and red subcaudal blotches identify the species.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Calliophis melanurus* is the presence of a distinct, large black blotch or "nuchal collar" on the nape, absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Slender Coral Snake inhabits moist deciduous forests and leaf litter in the Western Ghats and parts of the Indian peninsula, typically at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Slender Coral Snake is primarily nocturnal and secretive, often remaining hidden beneath leaf litter or soil to forage for small lizards and their eggs.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calliophis melanurus* is oviparous, laying small clutches of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Slender Coral Snake is found across peninsular India, primarily in the Western Ghats and parts of the Deccan Plateau, ranging from sea level to 1,200 meters.
